eligibility_reason: The paper reports original web-tracking estimates of exposure to and reach of untrustworthy news sites among German adults in 2017 and 2024.

estimates.measure: share of media diets consisting of visits to untrustworthy news sources
estimates.misinfo_definition: NewsGuard-classified untrustworthy websites with a score below 60 on a 0–100 reliability scale
estimates.source_quote: Visits to untrustworthy news sources make up less than 1% of media diets and are associated with low satisfaction with democracy and a preference for a far-right party.

estimates.measure: share who visited at least one untrustworthy news site
estimates.misinfo_definition: NewsGuard-classified untrustworthy websites with a score below 60 on a 0–100 reliability scale
estimates.source_quote: During the longer 2017 tracking window, 17% of participants visited at least one untrustworthy news site, compared to just 8% in the shorter 2024 period.

estimates.measure: share who visited at least one untrustworthy news site
estimates.misinfo_definition: NewsGuard-classified untrustworthy websites with a score below 60 on a 0–100 reliability scale
estimates.source_quote: During the longer 2017 tracking window, 17% of participants visited at least one untrustworthy news site, compared to just 8% in the shorter 2024 period.
estimates.notes: The table later reports 9% (6%–11%) for 2024; this estimate preserves the 8% printed in the main text.

estimates.denominator: all news visits by participants in 2017
estimates.measure: share of visits to untrustworthy news outlets among all news visits
estimates.misinfo_definition: NewsGuard-classified untrustworthy websites with a score below 60 on a 0–100 reliability scale
estimates.source_quote: We therefore focus on two alternative individual-level measures: the share of visits to untrustworthy news outlets among all news visits—0.75% in 2017 and 0.52% in 2024—and the average NewsGuard score (ranging from 0—lowest to 100—highest reliability) across all news visits, stable at 96 in both years.

estimates.denominator: all news visits by participants in 2024
estimates.measure: share of visits to untrustworthy news outlets among all news visits
estimates.misinfo_definition: NewsGuard-classified untrustworthy websites with a score below 60 on a 0–100 reliability scale
estimates.source_quote: We therefore focus on two alternative individual-level measures: the share of visits to untrustworthy news outlets among all news visits—0.75% in 2017 and 0.52% in 2024—and the average NewsGuard score (ranging from 0—lowest to 100—highest reliability) across all news visits, stable at 96 in both years.
